run.question: Debug memory issues for my Python application orca in namespace app-95

report.summary: The orca workload in namespace app-95 is being OOMKilled. Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-nvb6z (owned by ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, owned by Deployment orca) shows restartCount 1 with lastState terminated: reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-21T07:17:55Z, against a container memory limit of 128Mi. The previous container's own log shows memory held by 'processed_images'/'thumbnails' rising monotonically (26.6 MB at 20 images, 66.7 MB at 50, 91.3 MB at 70, 114.3 MB at 90) until it was killed while processing image 97. The replacement container in the same pod started at 07:17:56 and logged its configuration ('Storing all processed images for audit trail', 'Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval') and is again growing on the same trajectory (58.5 MB at 50 images by 07:18:01), so the workload is set to repeat the OOM. Only Normal scheduling/start events exist in the window; there is no Evicted, BackOff or Failed event and no pod-template change beyond the initial creation of the single ReplicaSet at 07:17:25. The container's 128Mi limit combined with retention that grows per processed image is the evidenced mechanism; the exact retention setting lives in the application code, which is mounted from a Secret that cannot be read, and Prometheus was unavailable for memory time series and restart counters, so those parts remain unverified.

claims.text: Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-nvb6z in namespace app-95, container 'orca', has restartCount 1 and lastState.terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 2026-11-21T07:17:26Z, finishedAt 2026-11-21T07:17:55Z; the container's memory limit is 128Mi and request 64Mi; current phase Running and ready=true.

The previous instance of the orca container logged a monotonically growing retained-memory figure while processing images: 'Approximate memory used by stored images: 26.6 MB' at 20 images (07:17:28), 41.3 MB at 30, 53.6 MB at 40, 66.7 MB at 50, 79.1 MB at 60, 91.3 MB at 70, 102.2 MB at 80, 114.3 MB at 90 (07:17:51), with matching 'Cache size: N thumbnails' and 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items' lines, and its last line was 'Processing image 97' at 07:17:55.114, immediately before the container was killed at 07:17:55Z.

The replacement instance of the same container started at 2026-11-21T07:17:56 in the same pod orca-57fdcbf45f-nvb6z and logged 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval', then repeated the same growth pattern: 11.4 MB at 10 images (07:17:57), 33.4 MB at 30, 46.9 MB at 40, 58.5 MB at 50 (07:18:01), still processing (image 52 at 07:18:02).

Deployment orca in namespace app-95 has 1 replica (1 ready/available, observedGeneration 1) with a single container 'orca' running image python:3.9-slim, command ['python','/app/app.py'], env PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and SERVICE_NAME=orca-image-processor, memory limit 128Mi / request 64Mi, and the application code mounted at /app from a Secret-backed volume whose secretName is redacted in the output.

Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-nvb6z is owned by ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, and that ReplicaSet is owned by Deployment orca; both the ReplicaSet and the pod were created at 2026-11-21T07:17:25Z, i.e. the container restart happened in place within the same pod, not as a new pod from a template change.

The events returned across all namespaces for the authorized window are 6 Normal events, all in namespace app-95: Pod Scheduled (07:17:25.480086Z), Pod Pulled (count 2, last 07:17:56), Pod Created (count 2, last 07:17:56), Pod Started (count 2, last 07:17:56), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate (07:17:25), Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 (07:17:25). No Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy event was returned.

The ConfigMap read for namespace app-95 returned exactly one object, kube-root-ca.crt (created 2026-11-21T07:17:25Z, containing only ca.crt); no ConfigMap holding orca application settings was returned for that namespace.

The OOM is caused by the orca application retaining every processed image and thumbnail without bound (its own 'processed_images list' and thumbnail cache, per its startup configuration lines and 10-image increment logs), giving roughly 1.1-1.3 MB of retained memory per processed image, so the container necessarily exceeds the 128Mi limit after roughly 95-100 images and is OOMKilled in a repeating cycle.

A contributing factor, not separable from the retention growth on this evidence, is that the 128Mi memory limit declared in Deployment orca is small relative to the amount of image data the service is configured to keep; a larger limit would delay but not remove the unbounded growth.

A pod rollout, eviction or node-level pressure was considered as the cause of the restart and is not supported: the pod name and ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f are unchanged from creation at 07:17:25, the restart is an in-place container restart (restartCount 1, lastState OOMKilled exitCode 137), and the window's events contain no SuccessfulDelete, Evicted, or FailedScheduling entry.

Bound the retention in the orca application (cap or TTL-evict the 'processed_images' list and thumbnail cache, or stop storing all processed images for the audit trail) so memory use stays flat instead of growing ~1.2 MB per image; then re-evaluate whether the 128Mi limit in Deployment orca is adequate for the bounded working set.

Add container memory visibility and alerting for app-95/orca (working-set time series and restart/OOM counters) since none were queryable in this Run, and add a readiness/liveness check so the repeated crash-restart cycle is detected rather than hidden behind a ready pod.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable in this Run: get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="app-95"}) and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no container_memory_working_set_bytes series, memory-limit series or restart-counter series could be checked; the growth pattern rests on the container's own log lines only.

The orca application code is mounted at /app from a Secret-backed volume (secretName redacted in the deployment/pod output); Secrets cannot be read, so the exact retention/caching settings and whether they are configurable or hard-coded could not be verified.

A cluster-wide query for ConfigMaps whose name matched 'orca' or whose keys matched IMAGE/CACHE/AUDIT/MEMORY returned no rows (status no_data), so it is unknown whether any settings for the service exist outside the unreadable Secret.

No OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Unhealthy Kubernetes event was returned for the pod; the OOM is evidenced only by status.containerStatuses.lastState and the container log, and the pod-deletion/kill reason is not present as an event.
Whether the current container (started 07:17:56, at 58.5 MB retained and image 52 at 07:18:02) has since been OOMKilled again is outside the sampled log window and unverified.

orca is not among the services Jaeger reports for this target (available services list does not include it), so no trace-based error or latency evidence for this workload was checked; impact beyond this single pod/replica is unobserved.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so whether the 'audit trail'/'thumbnail cache' configuration was changed recently cannot be established.
next_steps: Review the application code delivered in the app-code Secret (e.g. /app/app.py) for the processed_images list and thumbnail cache, and confirm whether a size cap or eviction policy exists and whether the audit-trail retention is configurable.

Compare container memory use with the processed-image count over a longer window once Prometheus is reachable, to confirm the per-image growth (~1.2 MB/image) and to see whether restarts repeat every ~100 images.

Decide with the service owner whether the intent is bounded caching (implement eviction) or full audit retention (move retained data out of process memory, e.g. object storage), then size the 128Mi limit accordingly.
